overview: This 254-page file compiles U.S. diplomatic and military reporting, translated party directives and press articles, memoirs, and intelligence assessments of Japanese communism from 1946 to 1949. It covers the Japan Communist Party’s leadership, elections, labor and press influence, party schools, alleged covert activity and Soviet links, political violence, and the revival of anti-communist groups. Some documents appear in duplicate.
interest: Translated leaders’ prison memoirs sit alongside U.S. intelligence assessments, revealing both Communist self-accounts and Occupation-era perceptions.
